answer.rationale: Rollback is ruled out by the non-revertible security patch. Circuit breaking is rejected because failing fast would drop customer writes, which violates the objective. Read-replica routing recovered write latency only when report/dashboard reads were loading the primary (b5); the live signal is peak settlement writes, not read offload, so that precedent is a weak match. Regional failover is not indicated and risks in-flight settlements. b3 is the closest fit: add write headroom so the peak can be absorbed without losing writes. Verifying b3 and b5 to check those precedents. Root cause (release vs. pure load) remains uncertain.
